en: Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great community of twelve hundred and fifty monks and about five thousand bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Blessed One, surrounded and venerated by an assembly of many hundreds of thousands, was teaching the Dharma.
Then Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, taking up a parasol measuring ten yojanas, held it over the head behind the Blessed One.

Then a son of the gods named Susīma, belonging to the Tuṣita host, who was irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment, having assembled there in that very assembly together with his retinue and being seated, rose from his seat, approached Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta, and having approached him, spoke thus to Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
"Even now, Mañjuśrī, you do not reach satiety in the act of making offerings to the Blessed One.
Mañjuśrī said: "What do you think, O son of the gods? Does the great ocean ever reach satiety from receiving water?
The son of the gods said: "Certainly not, Mañjuśrī."

Mañjuśrī said: "In just this way, O Devaputra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to seek the omniscient wisdom—which is like the great ocean, profound, difficult to fathom, immeasurable, and uncommon—must attain insatiable devotion toward making offerings specifically to the Tathāgata.
The Devaputra asked: "With what objective support, Mañjuśrī, should the Tathāgata be worshipped?"

Mañjuśrī said: "O sons of the gods, the Tathāgata should be honored by means of four objects of focus. What are these four? They are as follows: the object of focus that is the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), the object of focus that is the liberation of all sentient beings, the object of focus that is the non-interruption of the lineage of the Three Jewels, and the object of focus that is the purification of all Buddha-fields. O sons of the gods, it is by these four objects of focus that the Tathāgata should be honored."

Thus spoke Mañjuśrī, and the divine son Susīma, being uplifted in spirit, as well as those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the entire assembly—including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—rejoiced in what was spoken by Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta.
The fifteenth Mahāyāna sūtra, titled *The Exposition of Mañjuśrī*, is complete.
